lead.description: probability farther from the centre than a normal curve places there, as in a kurtosis above 3

self_checks.title: Two samples of five
self_checks.prompt: Using divisor n, what are the moment kurtoses of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and of 1, 1, 1, 1, 6?
self_checks.answer: The first kurtosis is 1.7 and the second is 3.25.

self_checks.title: An exponential tail
self_checks.prompt: For a unit exponential, what is the probability of exceeding 4, to six decimals, and what is the kurtosis of the law?
self_checks.answer: The probability is 0.018316 and the kurtosis is 9.

self_checks.title: Excess over the normal
self_checks.prompt: A unit exponential has kurtosis 9. What is the excess over the normal value 3, and what is the survival past 1?
self_checks.answer: The excess is 6. The survival past 1 is about 0.367879.

overview_sentence: [Fat tails](articles/fat-tails.qmd) put more probability far from the centre than a normal curve does.
